question.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Point or Segment
question.problem:
Consider the transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=2u-v,\,y=u+3v-1.
$$

Let $P(2,-2)$ be a point in the $uv$-plane. Suppose that the image of $P$ under the action of $T$ is the point ${P}^{′}$ in the $xy$-plane. What are the coordinates of ${P}^{′}?$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2u-v \\ u+3v-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2u-v \\ u+3v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the image of $P$ under the action of $T,$ we first create a column vector $u$ containing the coordinates of $P:$

$$
u=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Applying $T$ to $u,$ we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of ${P}^{′}$ are $(6,-5).$

question.problem:

Consider the segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ above, and the transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=v-2u-3,\,y=u+2v-1.
$$

The image of $\overset{―}{PQ}$ under the action of $T$ is the segment $\overset{―}{{P}^{′}{Q}^{′}}$ in the $xy$-plane. Which of the following diagrams shows $\overset{―}{{P}^{′}{Q}^{′}}?$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}v-2u-3 \\ u+2v-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2u+v \\ u+2v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the endpoints of $\overset{―}{PQ}$ to the endpoints of $\overset{―}{{P}^{′}{Q}^{′}}.$ So, to find the image of $\overset{―}{PQ},$ we find the images of each endpoint.

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing the endpoints of our segment:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -3 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 & -3 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 & -3 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -8 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the endpoints of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(0,0)$ and $(-8,-1).$

Drawing this segment in the $xy$-plane, we get the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/bce5c5155a7e8f1f257b85712627d44dfcc467911a6638016bc3df5892054fef.png)

question.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Polygon Under an Affine Transformation
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/838861910879e95b0e1c3055da9f9597f194950c3823867a20a1e3c149354437.png)

Consider the rectangle $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 2\}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
x=2u-v+1,\,y=u-v+1.
$$

Which of the following gives the image of $Δ$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2u-v+1 \\ u-v+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2u-v \\ u-v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/c89be48140d49ce8c9def44122aa2bfac779bdd02cfbfbe98f97d414a5637409.png)

          

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our square:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(1,1),(3,2),(1,0),$ and $(-1,-1).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/d038caec0aa360e5d8cc1bcb4a3aa4d88408496d947b312d47634e51bbf4a11f.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=-1<0,$ this transformation is not orientation-preserving.

evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(1,1),(3,2),(1,0),$ and $(-1,-1).$

question.knowledge_point: Determining the Area Scale Factor of an Affine Transformation
question.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

What is the area scale factor of the transformation?
question.worked_solution:
The matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].$ 

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|=1\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot 1=3.
$$

So, the area scale factor of the transformation is

$$
|det(A)|=|3|=3.
$$
